exampleCode:
import { createMongoAbility, AbilityBuilder } from '@casl/ability';
import { accessibleBy } from '@casl/mongoose';

// Define permissions once
const { can, cannot, build } = new AbilityBuilder(createMongoAbility);

can('read', ['Post', 'Comment']);
can('manage', 'Post', { author: 'me' });
can('create', 'Comment');

const ability = build();

// Enforce them across your application
ability.can('read', 'Post') // UI & API
accessibleBy(ability, 'update').ofType('Post') // Database conditions

evolution.title: A path from simple claims to relationships
evolution.intro: Add precision as your product evolves. Select a stage to explore.

claims.title: Claims
claims.description: Start with feature access or simple capabilities expressed as actions.
claims.example:
can('read:project');
can('update:project');
can('manage:workspace');
claims.detail: A stable API for simple permissions, ready to gain resource context when you need it.

actions.title: Actions / Subjects
actions.description: Give every layer a shared vocabulary: what action, on which resource?
actions.example:
can('read', 'Project');
can('update', 'Project');
can('manage', 'Workspace');
actions.detail: The same capability vocabulary now distinguishes articles, projects, and workspaces.

rbac.title: RBAC
rbac.description: Map roles to rules once, instead of scattering role checks across features.
rbac.example:
can('read', 'Project');
if (user.role === 'projectAdmin') can('update', 'Project');
if (user.role === 'workspaceAdmin') can('manage', 'Workspace');
rbac.detail: Roles become bundles of action/resource permissions.

abac.title: ABAC
abac.description: Refine permissions with ownership, tenant identity, or resource state.
abac.example:
can('read', 'Project', { tenantId: user.tenantId });
if (user.role === 'projectAdmin') {
  can('update', 'Project', { tenantId: user.tenantId });
}
if (user.role === 'workspaceAdmin') {
  can('manage', 'Workspace', { tenantId: user.tenantId });
}
abac.detail: Roles can still grant permissions; attributes constrain which records those grants cover.

rebac.title: ReBAC
rebac.description: Add workspace membership and resource administrator relationships on top of tenant isolation.

denormalized.label: Denormalized
denormalized.example:
can('read', 'Project', {
  tenantId: user.tenantId,
  workspaceMemberIds: { $in: [user.id] }
});

can('update', 'Project', {
  tenantId: user.tenantId,
  projectAdminIds: { $in: [user.id] }
});

can('manage', 'Workspace', {
  tenantId: user.tenantId,
  workspaceAdminIds: { $in: [user.id] }
});
denormalized.detail: Denormalized: Fast, local permission checks. Requires keeping derived membership attributes synchronized.

sql.label: SQL relations
sql.example:
can('read', 'Project', {
  tenantId: user.tenantId,
  workspace: {
    is: {
      memberships: { some: { userId: user.id } }
    }
  }
});

can('update', 'Project', {
  tenantId: user.tenantId,
  memberships: {
    some: { userId: user.id, role: 'projectAdmin' }
  }
});

can('manage', 'Workspace', {
  tenantId: user.tenantId,
  memberships: {
    some: { userId: user.id, role: 'workspaceAdmin' }
  }
});
sql.detail: SQL relations: Evaluate permissions through existing database relationships with @casl/prisma. No duplicated membership lists.

evolution.caption: Complementary models, not mandatory migrations. RBAC, ABAC, and relationship-derived permissions can coexist.
